chapter: Paul Mares and the Rhythm Kings
title: Jelly Roll Morton records with the Rhythm Kings
summary: Morton brought tunes to Paul, contributed to Milenberg Joys, and recorded with the band, a rare mixed session; Mares defends the band's Tin Roof Blues origin.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: the New Orleans Rhythm Kings were probably the most popular jazz band in the country Jelly Roll Morton was just floating around and really couldn't get too much work around there and he was plugging tunes for Melrose Brothers Melrose Brothers asked Jelly Roll at least told him to go see Paul Merez you got some nice tunes here and he's from New Orleans and Jelly Roll knew him and Jelly Roll came over to see Paul and told him about the tunes he had and so forth and Paul had a session coming up with Jeanette Records and Jelly Roll played a tune for him called Mr. Jelly Lord Paul liked it very well so Jelly Roll asked to come to the rehearsal and that they could go over this tune which he did and he had another tune called London Blues and that particular time Paul and Rap were going to record Millen Boy Joys they never had any first part to it voice and Jelly Roll put the first part to the Millen Boy Joys and they gave him part of it
I'd heard he wrote the introduction or something but the verse

is what I wrote the voice and they added that on to it and they gave Jelly Roll Martin a piece of tune lots of times you hear that Jelly Roll Martin gets grabbed for Millen Boy that's wrong because they played that way down here before they even left that same outfit and like the Tin Root Blues too they claim they stole that well that's not true because they played it way before they left here Georgie did and Paul and Rap they played that blues before they left New Orleans so they couldn't steal that
Richard M. Jones had once said he thought some of it was from
Jazz Baby Blues but it's not the same too it's not they were wrong on it
one part resembles it but it's not the same idea

well anyway Jelly Roll made the session with Paul and them which came out very very good and I think that was one of the first times that I can remember there's a lot of other times that was a chance for a colored fellow to sit in with a white band probably the first

to record it and it sounds funny being a New Orleans bunch but it did fit and if he could play music they didn't worry about his color or anything else and he did no one has to talk about Jelly Roll Martin he had a gold tooth and a diamond a lot of people knew that and don't know it but anyhow we could bring it out so Bill is there any other little questions or things you'd like to let's try to search
